name: Aditya Birla Capital Ltd
title: Aditya Birla Capital Ltd - 540691 - Analyst/Investor Meet- Transcript

read.thesis: Diversified lender-insurer with NBFC ROA 2.45% and credit cost 0.92%; supply-side signals are thin since no capacity or industry-capacity discussion, and margin expansion is guided only 'over a period'.

triggers.label: NBFC variable-rate book repriced +25 bps
triggers.quote: we have increased our benchmark rates by 25 bps effective 26th October on our variable rate loan book which constitutes nearly 70% of overall loan book
triggers.highlight: increased our benchmark rates by 25 bps

triggers.label: NBFC ROA to ~2.5% by Q4
triggers.quote: we had committed and guided the market that we will be closer to 2.5% ROA by quarter 4 of this financial year

triggers.label: Cost of funds up 11 bps QoQ
triggers.quote: So, if you look at between the incremental cost of borrowing between quarter 1 and quarter 2, it went up by 11 basis points.
triggers.highlight: it went up by 11 basis points

guidance.quote: we will be closer to 2.5% ROA by quarter 4 of this financial year
Our guidance continues to grow Individual FYP at a CAGR of 20%+ for the next 3 years

guidance.value: above 20%; double net VNB in 3 years
guidance.quote: we intend expand VNB margins above 20% and in absolute numbers double the value of our Net VNB in 3 years' time
We plan a phased rollout of 200-300 dedicated Gold Loan branches by March 2027
Over the next 8-10 quarters, we remain focused on building a ₹1 lakh crore plus AUM franchise
it should remain in this range of 1.85% to 1.9% even when we invest in our gold loan branches

red_flags.quote: We created some management overlay, but that's part of the overall credit cost

red_flags.label: Health insurer combined ratio 107%
red_flags.quote: The combined ratio in the health insurance business was 107%.

evasions.quote: Raghav, what happens is there are cycles and there are some quarters where the growth is much stronger than other quarters.
And margins will come over a period. See, again, we are not in a hurry to onboard high -risk customers to improve the margin.

evasions.quote: we'll have to wait and see what the final regulation turns out to be.

summary.headline: ABCL Q2 FY27 PAT rose 38% YoY to Rs 1,288 Cr on revenue of Rs 16,545 Cr; NBFC RoA reached 2.45% with credit cost at 0.92%.
summary.overview: Consolidated PAT of Rs 1,288 Cr grew 38% YoY and 10% QoQ, with revenue up 31% YoY to Rs 16,545 Cr. NBFC PAT rose 41% YoY to Rs 1,008 Cr with RoA of 2.45%, and credit cost improved to 0.92%, which management called its best in seven years. Housing finance PAT rose 73% YoY to Rs 261 Cr, and the company raised lending rates by 20-25 bps after the RBI repo action. Management also launched gold loans (AUM Rs 200 Cr after about 70 days) and continued AI rollout across businesses.

segments.name: NBFC
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 1,76,557 Cr (+26.5% YoY); Q2 sourcing Rs 24,708 Cr, near the record Q4 FY26. MSME AUM Rs 1,01,119 Cr (57% of book, 30% YoY), GS3 1.2%. Personal & consumer AUM Rs 24,955 Cr (+37% YoY), GS3 1.3%. Corporate 29% of book, GS3 1.6%.

segments.name: Housing finance (ABHFL)
segments.commentary: AUM Rs 57,373 Cr (+50% YoY); disbursements Rs 8,957 Cr (+55% YoY). GS2+3 at 0.65% and GS3 at 0.37%. Over 100 new branches launched so far this FY; target Rs 1 lakh Cr+ AUM in 8-10 quarters and 15% ROE.

segments.name: Asset management (ABSLAMC)
segments.commentary: Total average AUM Rs 11.06 lakh Cr (+140% YoY, including ESIC/EPFO mandates). Equity MF QAAUM Rs 2.09 lakh Cr (+9% YoY); passive QAAUM Rs 39,860 Cr; ETF QAAUM +42% YoY vs industry +27%. About 85% of funds in top quartile; SIF assets about Rs 700 Cr.

segments.name: Life insurance (ABSLI)
segments.commentary: H1 total premium Rs 12,656 Cr (+42%); individual APE growth 25% vs industry 12%. VNB margin 16.1%, solvency 190%. AUM Rs 1,20,736 Cr (+16% YoY). Guidance: 20%+ individual FYP CAGR for three years, VNB margin above 20%.

segments.name: Health insurance (ABHI)
segments.commentary: H1 GWP Rs 4,543 Cr (+48% YoY), market share 14.2% (from 13.6%). Retail +43% YoY, corporate +55% YoY. H1 FY27 profit Rs 46 Cr under IFRS; combined ratio 107%.

guidance_outlook: NBFC RoA targeted near 2.5% by Q4 FY27; management says it is already at 2.45%.
NBFC opex/AUM to stay around 1.85-1.9% even with gold loan branch investments.
NBFC margins expected to improve over a few quarters through mix shift, but management is not chasing high-risk customers to do so.
Expected Q3 cost of borrowing increase of 5-10 bps, following the 11 bps increase in Q2.
Life insurance guidance intact: 20%+ individual FYP CAGR, VNB margin above 20%, and net VNB doubling in three years.
Gold loans: 200-300 dedicated branches by March 2027, scaling to 1,000+ branches over three years.
capex_capacity: Gold loan business launched August 2026: about 70 branches opened and AUM Rs 200 Cr in the first ~70 days.
Housing finance: more than 100 new branches launched in the current fiscal year to date.
Life insurance plans to add people and branches in proprietary channel; IndusInd Bank onboarded as a bancassurance partner, with business commencement targeted for Q4 FY27.
GIFT City retail fund platform launched; about six more retail funds in the pipeline.
demand_pricing: NBFC retail/MSME focus: Retail and MSME were 71% of H1 disbursements vs 67% a year earlier; 85% of Q2 AUM addition came from these segments.
NBFC disbursements Rs 11,252 Cr for MSME (about 16% QoQ growth); unsecured business loans disbursed Rs 1,515 Cr (+9% QoQ).
NBFC raised benchmark lending rates by 25 bps effective 26 October on about 70% variable-rate book. HFC raised PLR by 20 bps effective 1 November.
Management said HFC BT-outs stay around 5-5.5% versus BT-ins about twice that; peers have also raised rates.
Life individual business: traditional/protection 66% and ULIP 34% of mix; annuity 14% of retail new business; partnership channel grew 31%, proprietary 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC retail disbursement growth moderate QoQ to about 12% versus the historical 20-30%, and was there pricing screening?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there was no slowdown and that retail is being calibrated to risk appetite; quarter-to-quarter variation is normal, personal & consumer AUM grew 37% YoY and unsecured business 53% YoY.

qa_highlights.question: Why did NBFC employee opex decline QoQ despite growth and new branches?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 had a one-off; Q2 normalised. Opex/AUM should stay at 1.85-1.9% even with gold loan branch investments.

qa_highlights.question: HFC cost of funds rose about 20 bps QoQ; was PLR raised?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds rose 11 bps (6.00% to 6.11%), partly from higher leverage after the April capital infusion; cost of borrowing was 7.46% in Q1 and 7.47% in Q2. PLR was raised 20 bps effective 1 November.

qa_highlights.question: Exposure to agri and drought-hit geographies, and outlook for the next two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: No direct agri exposure in the NBFC book; the main impact is indirect, through inflation and interest rates.

qa_highlights.question: Life insurance: how will bank relationships evolve under distribution reform and how will the opex-to-premium target be met?
qa_highlights.answer: Opex-to-premium is 21.2%. Management will wait for final regulation; growth is expected to lower the ratio. Direct channel is 8-9% of business (from 2-3%), and 98% of net VNB comes from individual business.

qa_highlights.question: NBFC ROA levers now that credit cost is below 1%, and when will disbursement yields feed into the book yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are growth, margin, opex and credit cost. Disbursement yields are well above portfolio yield, but the impact will take a few quarters to show in the book. Management expects ROA to stay near 2.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Cost of funds on book vs incremental basis after the rate hike, and any management overlay on credit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 57% of borrowings are floating and 30% of assets are fixed (70% floating), so repricing can pass through increases. A management overlay was created for stressed segments and sits within the 0.92% credit cost.

risks_watch: Rising rates and inflation (deficient monsoon, higher energy and food prices) could pressure borrowing costs and personal loan customers.
Life insurance and health distribution regulation: commission caps (EOM) and the consultation paper could compress margins and bank tie-ups.
Early-stage gold loan book (Rs 200 Cr) and its branch build-out (200-300 branches by March 2027) carry execution and credit risk.
Management says NBFC margins will improve only over a few quarters, so NIM expansion is not yet visible.
Health insurance combined ratio of 107% and profit of Rs 46 Cr in H1 under IFRS transition.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, asset quality and ROA, with explicit caution on the rate and inflation backdrop. Management was evasive on the life insurance regulation (EOM caps), saying it would wait for final rules, and on near-term NBFC margin expansion, which it framed as a multi-quarter story.
key_quotes: Despite volatile market conditions and uncertainties in operating environment, our asset quality across both lending businesses remains best -in class.
We already are almost there at 2.45% ROA in quarter 2.
So, we are quite focused on building a resilient book over a period and to answer your question on product mix, if you look at the unsecured mix, it has gone up by 1% over the last quarter.

growth.why: Management guides NBFC RoA near 2.5% by Q4 FY27 (already 2.45%), life individual FYP 20%+ CAGR and HFC AUM Rs 1 lakh Cr+ in 8-10 quarters; backing is partial, with gold loan branch rollout (200-300 by March 2027), 100+ HFC branches and bancassurance go-live, but no quantified capex or order figures.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management says NBFC margins improve over a few quarters via mix shift (70% floating book, 25 bps lending rate hike), but NIM expansion is not yet visible and Q3 cost of borrowing is guided up 5-10 bps; NBFC RoA is 2.45% vs ~2.5% target by Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Gold loan dedicated branches go from about 70 to 200-300 by March 2027 (1,000+ over 3 years), HFC has added 100+ branches this FY, and IndusInd bancassurance commencement is targeted for Q4 FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: NBFC AUM grew 26.5% YoY to Rs 1,76,557 Cr with Q2 sourcing Rs 24,708 Cr near record; HFC AUM +50% YoY; life individual APE growth 25% vs industry 12%; health GWP +48% YoY.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No capex amount or utilisation figure was given; the brief's capex read is 'not discussed'.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is guiding NBFC RoA to 'closer to 2.5%' by Q4 FY27 from 2.45% today, which is a held target rather than a raise, and it flagged rate and inflation pressure.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Rising rates and inflation (deficient monsoon, higher energy and food prices) could pressure borrowing costs (Q3 cost of borrowing +5-10 bps) and personal loan customers, while health combined ratio is 107%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Gold loan rollout is under way (about 70 branches, Rs 200 Cr AUM) and about six more GIFT City retail funds are in the pipeline.

rows.label: Life insurance 20%+ individual FYP CAGR and VNB margin above 20%
rows.why: Individual APE grew 25% vs industry 12% in H1 FY27, VNB margin 16.1% (+~450 bps YoY), and guidance held for 3 years.

rows.label: IndusInd Bank bancassurance partnership go-live
rows.why: IndusInd Bank is onboarded and business commencement is targeted for Q4 FY27, adding a bank distribution channel alongside the 31% partnership channel growth.

rows.label: Life and health distribution reform (EOM commission caps)
rows.why: Commission caps and the consultation paper could compress life and health margins and bank tie-ups; management is waiting for final rules, with opex-to-premium at 21.2%.

tone.note: Management was confident on growth, asset quality (credit cost 0.92%) and ROA (2.45%), and cautious on rates and inflation; analysts probed disbursement moderation, opex, cost of funds and EOM regulation, which management was evasive on, saying it would wait for final rules.
